title: La mission secrète de Renard  (Renard's Secret Mission)

segments.t: Outside the agency building, the preparations for the grand anniversary party are underway. Mathias approaches the security guard Renard to give him an urgent and confidential assignment. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Ça va, Renard?
Ça va, tout se passe bien.
J'ai une mission spéciale pour toi.
Je t'écoute attentivement, Mathias.
Deux invités américains vont arriver ce soir.
Tu as leurs noms précis?
Marcel Amos et Scott Downing.
À quelle heure arrivent-ils ici?
Ils arrivent précisément à vingt-deux heures.
Que dois-je faire exactement?
Préviens-moi dès leur arrivée en bas.
Cette affaire reste ultra confidentielle?
Oui, personne ne doit savoir cela.
Je garde le secret absolu.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Ça va, Renard?
'Are you alright, Renard?' Mathias greets the security guard. The familiar question 'how are things' is standard in French greetings.
Ça va, tout se passe bien.
'Everything is going fine.' Renard reports that all operations are running smoothly. The pronominal verb 'itself' means to happen or proceed.
J'ai une mission spéciale pour toi.
'I have a special mission for you.' Mathias entrusts him with a private assignment. The adjective 'special' emphasizes extraordinary importance.
Je t'écoute attentivement, Mathias.
'I am listening attentively, Mathias.' Renard gives his full attention. The adverb 'attentively' indicates careful focus.
Deux invités américains vont arriver ce soir.
'Two American guests will arrive tonight.' Mathias prepares for the VIP arrival. The near future 'are going to' describes an impending event.
Tu as leurs noms précis?
'Do you have their exact names?' Renard asks for clear identification details. The adjective 'exact' denotes distinct accuracy.
Marcel Amos et Scott Downing.
'Marcel Amos and Scott Downing.' Mathias names the two prominent film figures. Proper nouns identify specific individuals clearly.
À quelle heure arrivent-ils ici?
'At what time do they arrive here?' Renard inquires about the expected schedule. The interrogative phrase 'a quelle heure' asks for the exact time.
Ils arrivent précisément à vingt-deux heures.
'They arrive precisely at ten PM.' Mathias gives the specific hour of the meeting. In French, 22h is expressed as 'vingt-deux heures'.
Que dois-je faire exactement?
'What must I do exactly?' Renard asks for his exact instructions. The inverted modal question 'what' is very polite.
Préviens-moi dès leur arrivée en bas.
'Notify me as soon as they arrive downstairs.' Mathias gives clear orders. The imperative 'notify' demands prompt notification.
Cette affaire reste ultra confidentielle?
'Does this matter stay strictly confidential?' Renard checks the required level of discretion. The adjective 'confidential' describes sensitive private business.
Oui, personne ne doit savoir cela.
'Yes, nobody must know that.' Mathias confirms the need for total discretion. The negative pronoun 'nobody' signifies not a single person.
Je garde le secret absolu.

'I keep absolute secrecy.' Renard promises complete loyalty and confidentiality. The adjective 'absolute' means complete and unconditional. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Mathias secures Renard's cooperation for the secret arrival of the American executives. With the security guard on alert, Mathias's hidden scheme can proceed undisturbed. Now, let's review the scene one last time.
